title: Rice's Theorem as a Lawvere Instance
description: Formalizes Rice's theorem (1953) — no non-trivial semantic property of programs is decidable — as a direct consequence of Lawvere's fixed-point theorem. The core insight: a 'decidable' (Bool-valued point-surjective) universal evaluation is impossible because Bool.not has no fixed point, which Lawvere converts into a contradiction. Derives the classical Rice result via an axiomatized Kleene recursion theorem.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: ClassicalRiceModel axiomatizes Kleene's recursion theorem via two structure fields: h_compile (universality of semantics) and kleene_rec (semantic fixed-point theorem). These are mathematical hypotheses used in classical_rice_abstract; the other five theorems (abstract_rice through no_halting_model) are fully axiom-free.
originalContributions: abstract_rice: no Bool-evaluation structure can be point-surjective (direct from Lawvere)
rice_induced_obstruction: any d : Val → Bool applied to a point-surjective structure gives a non-surjective Bool structure
rice_undecidable_witness: for any Bool eval, there exists an undecidable function
semantic_rice_flip: a semantic property with a flip program leads to direct contradiction
no_halting_model: no abstract halting model with decidable universality exists
classical_rice_abstract: Rice's theorem from Kleene's recursion theorem (axiomatized)

overview.historicalContext:
Rice's theorem (1953) is one of the deepest results in computability theory: for any non-trivial semantic property P of partial computable functions (meaning P depends only on what a program computes, not how), the set {e | φ_e has property P} is undecidable. The classical proof uses Kleene's recursion theorem (1938), which itself is a consequence of the self-referential diagonal construction at the heart of Cantor's argument.

Lawvere (1969) unified all such diagonal arguments categorically: in any cartesian closed category, a point-surjective morphism forces every endomorphism to have a fixed point. Since Bool.not has no fixed point, no point-surjective Bool evaluation can exist — this is the abstract essence of Rice's theorem.

This file answers Open Question OQ-02 from CantorDiagonalizationOQ03OQ01: 'Derive Rice's theorem as a Lawvere instance.'
overview.problemStatement:
Formalize Rice's theorem via the Lawvere fixed-point framework:
1. Show that no Bool-valued evaluation structure is point-surjective (abstract Rice core)
2. Derive that no decision procedure can universally classify program behaviors
3. Prove the classical Rice theorem from Kleene's recursion theorem
4. Connect the halting problem as the canonical undecidable Rice instance
overview.proofStrategy:
**Step 1** (Bool Lawvere): Apply lawvere_fpt with f = Bool.not to any putative point-surjective Bool eval structure. Since Bool.not has no fixed point (cases v; simp), we get a contradiction.

**Step 2** (Induced obstruction): For any d : Val → Bool, the structure (Ob, Bool, d ∘ eval) has Val = Bool, so Step 1 applies directly.

**Step 3** (Semantic flip): If a semantic property P has a 'flip program' (same semantics, opposite property), the semantic-respecting condition immediately gives P(flip a) = P a (via semantics) while flip_prop gives P(flip a) ≠ P a — direct contradiction.

**Step 4** (Classical Rice): Axiomatize Kleene's recursion theorem. Define a 'flipper' code transformer f(e) = (if P(e) then e₀ else e₁). Kleene gives a semantic fixed point e* with semantics(f(e*)) = semantics(e*). Since P is semantic, P(e*) = P(f(e*)). But f flips P by definition — contradiction.
keyInsights: Bool.not having no fixed point is the computational content of Rice's theorem
Point-surjectivity (universality of evaluation) + Bool → fixed-point paradox = Rice
The semantic property + flip program argument doesn't even need point-surjectivity — direct contradiction
Kleene's recursion theorem is the bridge from abstract Lawvere to the classical Rice statement
HaltingModel as a special case: a decidable universal halting predicate is exactly a point-surjective Bool eval structure
prerequisites: Bool arithmetic: Bool.not has no fixed point

sections.title: Imports and Module Overview
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib.Logic.Function.Basic and Mathlib.Tactic, then provides a comprehensive docstring describing the three-layer proof architecture: Abstract Rice (Bool Lawvere), Semantic Rice (flip program), and Kleene-Rice (classical computability theorem).

sections.title: Evaluation Structure Framework
sections.summary: Defines EvalStructure (a triple of programs, values, and evaluation), IsPointSurjective (every function Ob → Val is represented by some code), and proves the Lawvere Fixed-Point Theorem: point-surjectivity forces every endomorphism to have a fixed point.

sections.title: Abstract Rice Theorem
sections.summary: Proves abstract_rice (no Bool-evaluation can be point-surjective, since Bool.not has no fixed point), rice_induced_obstruction (composition with any d : Val → Bool inherits this obstruction), and rice_undecidable_witness (for every eval, there exists a Bool function no code can represent).

sections.title: Semantic Properties and Flip Programs
sections.summary: Defines SemanticProperty (extensional: programs with equal behavior have equal property value) and HasFlipProgram (a total transformer that inverts the property). Proves semantic_rice_flip: a semantic property with a same-semantics flip transformer is immediately contradictory — no point-surjectivity needed.

sections.title: The Halting Problem as Rice Instance
sections.summary: Defines HaltingModel (programs, halts predicate, evaluate, and decidable-universality axiom) and proves no_halting_model: no such model exists, because M.universal is exactly the point-surjectivity condition that abstract_rice refutes.

sections.title: Classical Rice Theorem (Axiomatized)
sections.summary: Defines ClassicalRiceModel axiomatizing Kleene's recursion theorem (every code transformer has a semantic fixed point). Proves classical_rice_abstract: any non-trivial semantic property leads to a flipper whose Kleene fixed point simultaneously satisfies and violates the property.

sections.title: Summary Type Checks
sections.summary: Six #check commands verify the types of all main theorems: abstract_rice, rice_induced_obstruction, rice_undecidable_witness, semantic_rice_flip, no_halting_model, and classical_rice_abstract.

conclusion.summary: Proved Rice's theorem as a Lawvere instance: no Bool-valued evaluation structure is point-surjective, which is the abstract essence of Rice's undecidability theorem. Derived 5 concrete results — abstract Rice, induced obstruction, undecidable witness, semantic flip, and no halting model — plus the classical Rice theorem from axiomatized Kleene recursion. 6 theorems, 0 axioms, 275 lines.
conclusion.implications: This file completes the Lawvere fixed-point theorem application chain: Cantor (Prop, negation) → Rice (Bool, not) → Gödel (sentences, negation of provability). The key insight is that undecidability results in computability theory are not independent of diagonal arguments in set theory — they all share the same Lawvere fixed-point core. The `classical_rice_abstract` theorem shows that Rice follows from Kleene's recursion theorem, which in turn follows from the same diagonal construction.
openQuestions: Formalize Kleene's recursion theorem without axiomatization: implement a concrete computation model (e.g., partial recursive functions or a simple lambda calculus) in Lean and prove the s-m-n theorem + universality, deriving Kleene recursion as a proved theorem rather than an axiom

Gödel's incompleteness as a Lawvere instance (OQ-03): extend the framework to formal proof systems where Val = formal sentences and the 'fixed-point' endomorphism is negation of provability, giving the diagonal lemma and Gödel's theorems

sections.title: Part I: Evaluation Structure and Lawvere Fixed-Point Theorem
sections.summary: Defines EvalStructure (programs, values, eval), IsPointSurjective (universal representation property), and proves lawvere_fpt: point-surjectivity forces every endomorphism to have a fixed point.
sections.mathContext: An evaluation structure $E = (A, V, \text{eval})$ is point-surjective if $\forall g: A \to V, \exists a_0, \forall x, \text{eval}(a_0, x) = g(x)$. The Lawvere fixed-point theorem: if $E$ is point-surjective, every $f: V \to V$ has a fixed point. Proof: choose $a_0$ representing $x \mapsto f(\text{eval}(x,x))$; then $f(\text{eval}(a_0, a_0)) = \text{eval}(a_0, a_0)$.

sections.title: Part II: Abstract Rice Theorem — Bool Lawvere
sections.summary: abstract_rice: no Bool eval is point-surjective (Bool.not has no fixed point). rice_induced_obstruction: any decision function d applied to a point-surjective structure is still not point-surjective over Bool. rice_undecidable_witness: for any decision procedure, an undecidable Bool function exists.
sections.mathContext: Since $\lnot : \text{Bool} \to \text{Bool}$ has no fixed point ($\lnot \text{false} \neq \text{false}$, $\lnot \text{true} \neq \text{true}$), no Bool eval structure can be point-surjective by Lawvere. Any $d: V \to \text{Bool}$ converts a $V$-structure to a Bool-structure, which is also non-point-surjective: always $\exists f: A \to \text{Bool}$ that no code can decide.

sections.title: Part III: Semantic Properties and Flip Programs
sections.summary: Defines SemanticProperty (P respects extensional equality) and HasFlipProgram (program transformer that inverts P). semantic_rice_flip proves: if P is semantic and has a flip program with same semantics but opposite property value, contradiction follows directly without needing Lawvere.
sections.mathContext: $P$ is semantic if $\forall a, b: \text{eval}(a,x) = \text{eval}(b,x)$ for all $x$ implies $P(a) = P(b)$. A flip $f$ satisfies $\text{eval}(f(a),x) = \text{eval}(a,x)$ (same semantics) and $P(f(a)) \neq P(a)$ (opposite property). Semantic-respecting gives $P(f(a)) = P(a)$ by the extensionality condition, contradicting the flip property.

sections.title: Part IV: The Halting Problem as a Rice Instance
sections.summary: HaltingModel structure packages programs, halts predicate, evaluate function, and a universal field asserting every Bool function of programs is computable. no_halting_model proves this structure cannot exist — its universal field is exactly point-surjectivity of the halting eval structure.
sections.mathContext: A `HaltingModel` with a `universal` field asserts: $\forall f: \text{Prog} \to \text{Bool}, \exists e, \forall x, \text{halts}(e,x) = f(x)$. This is point-surjectivity of $(\text{Prog}, \text{Bool}, \text{halts})$. By `abstract_rice`, this is impossible. The proof is one line: `abstract_rice M.Prog M.halts M.universal`.

sections.title: Part V: Classical Rice Theorem via Kleene Recursion
sections.summary: ClassicalRiceModel axiomatizes programs, behaviors, semantics, compile (behavior → code), and Kleene's recursion theorem. classical_rice_abstract proves: any semantic, non-trivial P : Code → Bool leads to contradiction via the flipper function and Kleene's fixed point.
sections.mathContext: Define flipper $f(e) = e_0$ if $P(e) = \text{true}$, else $e_1$. Kleene gives $e^*$ with $\text{semantics}(f(e^*)) = \text{semantics}(e^*)$. Semantic-respecting: $P(e^*) = P(f(e^*))$. But by definition $f$ always flips $P$: $P(f(e^*)) \neq P(e^*)$. Contradiction. The flipper is the Lawvere endomorphism in disguise: it maps $\text{true} \mapsto \text{false}$ and $\text{false} \mapsto \text{true}$ via $e_0, e_1$.
